text: Kim's causal exclusion argument turns on four jointly inconsistent principles: the causal efficacy of the mental, the causal closure of the physical, the denial of systematic overdetermination, and which fourth?
choices: The multiple realizability of mental properties.
The supervenience of the mental on the physical.
The non-reduction (non-identity) of mental properties to physical properties.
explanation: Kim's tetrad is mental causation, physical causal closure, no systematic overdetermination, and non-reduction; these cannot all be true, so the non-reductive physicalist must either reduce the mental (drop non-reduction) or accept epiphenomenalism. Supervenience is assumed by non-reductive physicalism but is not one of the four inconsistent principles, and multiple realizability is the motivation for non-reduction rather than a member of the tetrad.
